requirement:
Sections use `section`, named from whitespace-normalized heading text. ATX and
setext headings are supported. Content before the first heading can form an
anonymous section. Section nesting follows heading levels; other outline items
appear beneath their nearest enclosing container. Selectors follow
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`.
rationale:
The tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.sections`, and I found no gaps. I did not request implementation source.

- **Kind `section` and whitespace-normalized names.**
  - `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs`) turns `# Head  *one*` into `section[Head%20*one*]`.
  - `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble` turns `Heading   words` into `section[Heading%20words]`.
  - `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` turns a two-line setext heading into `section[Títle%20two]`. This shows line breaks and runs of spaces collapse to one space.
- **ATX and setext headings.**
  - ATX headings are covered in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items` and `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading`.
  - Setext `===` and `---` headings are covered in `markdown_sections_include_setext_headings_and_anonymous_preamble`, `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` and the heading-levels test.
  - `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans` covers setext headings inside directives, block quotes and lists.
  - `multiline_setext_sections_keep_original_source_spans_and_skip_code` checks that `===` inside a code fence is not treated as a heading.
- **Anonymous section before the first heading.**
  - The heading-levels test and the preamble test assert an anonymous `section@…` for `préface` and `intro`.
  - The `src/outline/tests.rs` test covers the same case, with front matter ahead of the preamble.
- **Nesting by heading level.**
  - `###` under `#`, which skips a level, is asserted in the heading-levels test.
  - Duplicate siblings `Same#1` and `Same#2` are asserted there too.
  - A return to `# End` and a setext level-2 section under it are covered, as is `## Peer` after that setext section.
  - Sections end where the next same-or-higher heading begins: the `Same#2` text excludes `first`, and the `Parent/Títle two` section excludes `# Last`.
- **Other outline items beneath the nearest enclosing container.**
  - Paragraphs sit under the section in `markdown_profile_nests_sections_by_heading`.
  - The `block@` directive sits under `section[End]/section[Level%20two]` in the heading-levels test.
  - `paragraphs_and_nested_directives_have_independent_source_ranges` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs`) checks parent indices for sections, blocks and nested paragraphs.
  - `setext_sections_inside_directives_lists_and_quotes_retain_container_spans` checks section and block nesting.
- **Selectors follow `requirements.references.outline_selectors`.**
  - Percent-encoding of `/`, `[`, `]`, `#`, `@` and `%` is checked in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`.
  - `#N` duplicate suffixes are checked there too.
  - Every selector is resolved back with `select` and `resolve`, so the selectors round-trip.

Untested inputs are ATX closing `#` sequences and tabs as whitespace. The requirement doesn't state either, so I don't count them as gaps. The assertions check exact selectors and span text, so a wrong name, level, nesting or section extent would fail them.
